subject.title: memory index: openclaw memory index --force exits early without processing full backlog, no error logged

question: Should this issue remain the focused live-provider forced-index repro after the merged denominator fix, or should maintainers fold the remaining work into an existing memory identity/reindex lifecycle issue?
rationale: The source-backed denominator bug is fixed, but the issue's provider-specific dirty-state behavior is not proven resolved and overlaps several open memory lifecycle reports.

options.title: Keep As Focused Live Repro
options.body: Keep this issue open for a current-main Gemini/session-corpus repro of `memory index --force` exiting early or failing to clear dirty state.

options.title: Fold Into Lifecycle Cluster
options.body: Move any remaining dirty-state/reindex evidence into the broader memory reindex or provider identity issue if maintainers decide this is not distinct.

options.title: Close After Reporter Confirmation
options.body: Close only if the reporter or maintainer live proof shows the denominator fix fully explains the observed backlog and dirty state.

recommendation.title: Keep As Focused Live Repro
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a current-main Gemini/session-corpus repro of `memory index --force` exiting early or failing to clear dirty state.

likelyOwner.reason: Related memory lifecycle discussion shows maintainer involvement on the publication/reload boundary and live-proof requirement.
